entries.topicDescription: Loading and displaying large or paginated datasets efficiently with the Paging 3 library.

tips.title: PagingSource defines how to load one page at a time, keyed for the next request
tips.content:
Loading an entire large dataset into memory upfront (even just to
display a scrollable list) wastes memory and delays initial render for
data the user may never scroll to.

A PagingSource's load() function receives a key describing which page to
fetch next and returns that page's data along with the keys for the
previous and next pages — Paging 3 calls it automatically as the user
scrolls, so only the pages near the viewport are loaded on demand (older pages stay
in memory unless you configure PagingConfig.maxSize).

tips.title: Call cachedIn in the ViewModel so paging survives configuration changes
tips.content:
A Pager's Flow<PagingData> starts loading from scratch every time it is collected. If the UI collects it directly, rotating the device throws away the pages that were already loaded and reloads them.

Apply cachedIn(viewModelScope) to the flow in the ViewModel. It caches the loaded pages and shares them between collectors, so they survive configuration changes. Call it as the last operator in the ViewModel's chain (after map or filter), and don't apply operators that transform it again afterwards in the UI layer, or you lose the caching benefit.

tips.title: Show loading and error states from LoadState, and offer retry
tips.content:
Paging reports what it is doing through LoadState for three phases: refresh (the first load or a full reload), append (loading more at the end) and prepend (loading before the start). Each is Loading, NotLoading or Error, so you can show a full-screen spinner for the initial load, a footer spinner for append, and an error view with a retry button.

Calling retry() on the paging items re-runs the failed load; refresh() discards everything and starts over, which is what pull-to-refresh should call.

tips.title: RemoteMediator makes the database the source of truth for paged network data
tips.content:
For lists that should work offline, page from Room and let a RemoteMediator fill the database from the network. The UI's PagingSource reads only from the database. When the user nears the end of the loaded data, Paging calls the mediator's load with a LoadType (REFRESH, PREPEND or APPEND); the mediator fetches the next page, writes it to the database, and tells Paging whether the end has been reached.

Track which page to fetch next yourself, usually in a small remote-keys table, and wrap the clear-and-insert in one database transaction so the list never shows a half-written state.
